title: King's Indian Set-up
intro: Against 1...Nf6 and ...g6, control e5 with Bf4, build calmly with e3, Be2 and h3, and tuck your bishop away on h2.

lessons.title: The calm London against ...g6
lessons.summary: Develop Bf4, e3 and Be2 against Black's fianchetto.

steps.text: When Black opens with 1...Nf6 and ...g6, there is no pawn on d5. Your London set-up still works smoothly.

steps.hint: Push the d-pawn, then develop the king's knight.

steps.text: Bring out your dark-squared bishop to control e5.
steps.hint: Put the bishop on f4 before e3.
steps.ifRight: The bishop sits on a great diagonal.

steps.text: Black puts the bishop on the long diagonal with 3...Bg7.
Open the way for your other bishop and strengthen d4.
steps.ifRight: White prepares Be2, h3 and castling.

steps.text: Black castles: 4...O-O. Develop your light-squared bishop to a safe square.
steps.hint: Put the bishop on e2, where it guards against ...Bg4 pins.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.Be2: against ...g6, the bishop sits better on e2 than on d3.
steps.ifRight: On e2, the bishop stops ...Bg4 pins and lets White castle.

feedback.f1d3: Bd3 is playable, though against ...g6 and ...d6 Black can target it with ...e5 or ...Bf5. Be2 is calmer and safer.

lessons.title: Saving the bishop with h3
lessons.summary: Create the h2 hideout before ...Nh5 arrives.

steps.text: Black plays 5...d6 and threatens ...Nh5 to trap and trade off your active f4 bishop.
Give your bishop a safe retreat square.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.h3 so your bishop can step back to h2.
steps.ifRight: Now your bishop can never be hunted down on f4.

steps.text: Tuck your king away to safety.
steps.ifRight: With the king safe, White finishes with c3 or c4 and Nbd2.

steps.text: If Black jumps in with 6...Nh5 anyway, the h2 square is waiting.

steps.hint: Retreat along the diagonal to h2.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7.Bh2: the bishop stays on its strong diagonal and Black's knight is awkward on h5.
steps.ifRight: The bishop is safe and Black wasted time with the knight.

lessons.title: Meeting ...c5 and ...e5
lessons.summary: Hold d4 with c3 and answer central breaks cleanly.

steps.text: Black can strike at your centre with 6...c5 instead of ...Nbd7.
Support d4 so the g7 bishop never hits b2.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7.c3: your d4 pawn is rock solid and b2 is safe.
steps.ifRight: Notice how c3 blocks the g7 bishop's diagonal.

steps.text: Castle to safety before opening lines.
steps.ifRight: Next White plays Nbd2 and meets ...e5 calmly.

steps.text: Black trades on d4 with 8...cxd4. Choose the stronger recapture.
steps.hint: Take back with the e-pawn to keep your queenside sound.
steps.ifWrong: Play 9.exd4: it opens the e-file and keeps b2 safe.
steps.ifRight: The e-file opens for your rook and d4 stays firmly supported by c3.

feedback.c3d4: 9.cxd4 weakens b2 and lets Black play against your queenside. 9.exd4 keeps the centre solid.

steps.text: Black finally pushes 9...e5. Answer the central break cleanly.
steps.hint: Take on e5 with the d-pawn, or tuck the bishop back to h2.
steps.ifWrong: Play 10.dxe5 (or 10.Bh2): taking on e5 opens the d-file for your pieces.
steps.ifRight: After 10.dxe5 dxe5 11.Bh2, White's pieces enjoy clear squares.
